prompt:
A full-fidelity desktop website homepage design comp, landscape, shown flat with no browser frame and no device. This is the website of a Christian nonprofit that provides reconstructive plastic surgery, free or at reduced cost, executed as a polished, conventional nonprofit site. Palette: deep navy, warm gold, ivory, white. Layout:

1. NAVIGATION over the top of the hero photo: at left a text wordmark "Beauty From Ashes" with "SURGICAL MINISTRY" in small spaced capitals; links "Our Mission", "How We Help", "Stories", "Get Involved", "Contact"; at right "EN | ES" and a gold button "Give".

2. HERO (60% of height): a full-bleed warm documentary-style photograph of a bright consultation room in soft morning window light, where a surgeon in navy scrubs sits at eye level talking with a smiling mother and her young daughter. A soft navy shade on the left third carries the text: small spaced-capitals eyebrow "A CHRISTIAN SURGICAL MINISTRY · CHARLOTTE & FORT MILL", a large white refined serif headline "Restoring more than what can be seen.", a paragraph "Reconstructive plastic surgery, free or at reduced cost, for children and adults whose need exceeds their means. Open to everyone.", a solid gold button "Ask for help" and a white outlined button "Refer someone".

3. VALUES (ivory band): centered small gold spaced capitals "OUR CORE VALUES", then six columns each with a thin gold line icon, a navy heading and one line: "We Listen." / "We give every patient the time their story deserves." — "We Protect." / "We hold patient safety as our highest surgical standard." — "We Pray." / "We pray with every patient who welcomes it." — "We Accompany." / "We walk with every patient long after surgery ends." — "We Honor." / "We honor the sacrifice behind every patient's decision." — "We Serve." / "We extend surgical care where need exceeds means."

Overall: hopeful, polished, professional; crisp legible web typography.
